summary: The retrieved content includes the implementation of a Binary Search algorithm in JavaScript, along with a numeric sort function. The Binary Search function recursively searches for an item in a sorted array by dividing the search interval in half and comparing the search item with the middle element of the interval.
purpose: The purpose of the content is to provide a JavaScript implementation of a Binary Search algorithm for efficiently finding elements within a sorted array.

workflows.name: Binary Search Execution
steps: Invoke the BinarySearch function with the search item, starting position, ending position, and the array.
Check if the start position equals the end position; if true, compare the search item with the element at the start position.
If the search item is equal to the element at the start position, return the start position; otherwise, return -1.
If the start position is greater than the end position, return -1.
Calculate the midPoint as the average of the startPos and endPos.
Compare the search item with the element at the midPoint.
If the search item is equal to the element at the midPoint, return the midPoint.
If the search item is less than the element at the midPoint, recursively call BinarySearch with updated end position (midPoint - 1).
If the search item is greater than the element at the midPoint, recursively call BinarySearch with updated start position (midPoint + 1).

system_behavior: Returns the index position of the search item if found.
Returns -1 if the search item is not found.
